messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The three main components of the Action Search model architecture are the visual encoder, the LSTM, and the fully-connected layer." -- cites: E5 (Figure 3): quote "At each step, (i) a visual encoder transforms the visual observation extracted from the model’s current temporal location to a representative feature vector; (ii) an LSTM consumes this feature vector plus the state and temporal location produced in the previous step; (iii) the LSTM outputs its updated state and the next search location; (iv) the model moves to the new temporal location."

Cited evidence:
[E5] (figure, Figure 3, page 7) (image attached): Fig. 3: Our model harnesses the temporal context from its current location and the history of what it has observed to predict the next search location in the video. At each step, (i) a visual encoder transforms the visual observation ex- tracted from the model’s current temporal location to a representative feature vector; (ii) an LSTM consumes this feature vector plus the state and temporal location produced in the previous step; (iii) the LSTM outputs its updated state and the next search location; (iv) the model moves to the new temporal location.

verdicts.reason: The cited evidence from E5 (Figure 3) describes the three main components of the Action Search model architecture: the visual encoder, the LSTM, and the fully-connected layer. The evidence explicitly mentions the visual encoder, LSTM, and the next search location, which aligns with the claim.
